paper_metadata.title: Predictors of seizure outcome in newly diagnosed partial epilepsy: memory performance as a prognostic factor

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study recruited a consecutive sample of untreated adult patients with a clearly defined diagnosis. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are explicit, and baseline characteristics are well-described for both the study groups and a healthy control group.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Eighty-nine consecutive untreated adult patients, aged between 15 and 63 years, with newly diagnosed partial epilepsy were included in the study.
items.reasoning: The population is clearly defined as adults with newly diagnosed partial epilepsy, including age range and treatment status.

items.evidence_snippet: Eighty-nine consecutive untreated adult patients... were included in the study.
items.reasoning: Use of consecutive recruitment in a clinical setting helps minimize selection bias.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Patients with alcohol-related seizures, current alcohol or other drug abuse, progressive neurological disorders, mental retardation, severe psychiatric problems, or other severe medical disorders were excluded from the study.
items.reasoning: Detailed exclusion criteria are provided to ensure a homogeneous sample of partial epilepsy.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (Memory, EEG, Clinical) were measured using standardized, validated tools (WMS, WAIS, ILAE classification) before treatment began, ensuring no influence of the outcome on the measurement.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The List Learning Test was used to assess learning and recall of words. It is a modification of the Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test (Lezak, 1995).
items.reasoning: The memory tests and EEG scoring criteria are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: The same neurophysiologist (E.M.), without knowledge of the clinical details, scored the EEG using criteria presented by Engel (1984).
items.reasoning: Standardized neuropsychological tests were used, and EEG scoring was blinded to clinical details.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The patients were classified as having clinically significant memory impairment when memory test scores were falling two standard deviations below the mean performance of the control group
items.reasoning: The study used a standard clinical threshold (2 SD) rather than an arbitrary data-driven cut-point.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Subjects underwent a full neurological examination... a comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation and electroencephalography (EEG) before starting antiepileptic drug treatment.
items.reasoning: All patients underwent the same standardized protocol at baseline.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (refractory vs. controlled) is defined by seizure frequency, which relies on patient self-reporting (seizure diaries), introducing potential recall bias. However, the criteria for 'refractory' were clearly pre-specified.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The seizure disorder was termed refractory if more than one generalized or more than four partial seizures occurred during 1 year.
items.reasoning: The study provides a specific, quantitative definition for the primary outcome.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: Group I patients had satisfactorily controlled epilepsy (seizure free or only occasional seizures), and Group II patients had refractory seizure disorder
items.reasoning: Outcome is based on clinical follow-up and seizure counts, which are standard but subject to patient reporting bias. Blinding of the outcome assessor to baseline memory scores is not explicitly stated.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: After a prospective 2-year follow-up period, the patients were divided into two groups
items.reasoning: All patients were followed for the same 2-year duration using the same clinical criteria.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study uses multivariable logistic regression to account for several key confounders (age, etiology, seizure type), the small number of events in the refractory group (n=10) limits the robustness of the adjustment and increases the risk of overfitting.

items.evidence_snippet: The following clinical variables were included in the analyses... age at the time of the diagnosis; etiology of epilepsy... seizure type... pretreatment number of seizures... EEG data
items.reasoning: Major known clinical prognostic factors were collected.

items.evidence_snippet: etiology of epilepsy, classified as remote symptomatic or cryptogenic; seizure type, subjects were categorized as having experienced either generalized seizures alone, or having experienced partial complex or mixed seizure types
items.reasoning: Confounders are categorized using standard neurological definitions.

items.reasoning: Confounders were measured using objective diagnostic tools (MRI/CT/EEG).

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).

items.reasoning: The study is a prospective cohort; no matching or stratification was used in the design phase.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: A backward stepwise logistic regression analysis was performed for clinical, neuropsychological and EEG variables.
items.reasoning: Multivariable adjustment was performed, but the small sample size of the refractory group (n=10) makes the model unstable (overfitting risk).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is generally sound, but the authors acknowledge the limitation of the small sample size in the refractory group, which resulted in very wide confidence intervals for the odds ratios, reducing the precision of the findings.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy

items.evidence_snippet: The data were analyzed by using SPSS/PC+... Logistic regression analysis is suitable for analyzing predictors of a binary outcome variable
items.reasoning: The statistical methods are clearly described.

items.label: Model development strategy

items.evidence_snippet: Five clinical and EEG variables, identified from the literature, three verbal memory measures, identified by univariate analyses... were included in logistic regression analysis.
items.reasoning: Variable selection was based on both prior literature and preliminary univariate findings.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: A backward stepwise logistic regression analysis was performed
items.reasoning: Logistic regression is appropriate for the binary outcome (refractory vs. controlled).
